item.title: Crew goes missing after ship sinks in Black Sea Zone of Bulgaria following drone strike, says PM
item.description: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Tuesday (local time) said that the crew of a ship that sunk following a drone strike in the country's Black Sea Zone is missing, Reuters reported.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev on Tuesday (local time) said that the crew of a ship that sank following a drone strike in the country's Black Sea zone is missing, AFP reported.Speaking to reporters, Radev condemned the drone attack on two commercial ships, calling it "a flagrant violation of maritime law". He added, "Such an attack within the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable." Here's what we knowHis remarks came shortly after local media reported that drones struck two commercial vessels in the Black Sea off the coast of Bulgaria, sinking one of them. After convening an emergency meeting on Tuesday, Radev stated that the ships were attacked by several drones roughly 80 miles (128km) off Bulgaria's coast.Rumen Nikolov, head of local rescue operations in Varna, was quoted as saying that sailors from the sunken ship were missing, while those aboard the second vessel were rescued, AFP reported.Rescue teams were searching for the missing sailors about 150 kilometres (90 miles) east of the coastal city of Byala. At least 18 crew members from the other vessel were evacuated by a Bulgarian ferry following the strikes. Of the evacuated members, two suffered severe injuries and were flown to a hospital in the port city of Varna, Radev stated.Radev said the Togo-flagged vessel Alfa Watan sustained severe structural damage in the strike and sank at the site, while the status of its crew remained unclear.British maritime security and risk consultancy Vanguard said two cargo ships were targeted by drones on Tuesday while operating within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, according to Reuters.The vessels involved were the Togo-flagged general cargo ship ALFA WATAN and the Palau-flagged ABLE. According to Vanguard, both ships sent distress alerts after the attacks, while Bulgarian sources told Reuters that drones had struck the vessels.The latest incident comes a day after Romanian authorities reported that two people were killed in a fire aboard a ship in the Black Sea, outside Romania’s territorial waters.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy attributed that incident to Russian drone attacks. Russia had not immediately commented on the allegation. The Black Sea has faced growing security risks since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Several European nations have since reported incidents involving Russian drones entering their airspace, while sea mines have also been detected in the Black Sea, affecting key trade and energy routes. Last month, Turkey's Chamber of Maritime Commerce (IMEAK) said that 226 civilian and commercial ships had come under attack in the Black Sea since the war began, with most of the incidents recorded this year.
